identityAssessment.finding: The imported Agwarmin record occupies northern Queensland, about 142.93 to 144.81 degrees east and 19.63 to 16.49 degrees south, matching the broad Gilbert and Einasleigh regional association. This establishes the intended identity, not precise boundaries or a native title determination polygon.

scopeNotes: The imported coverage is 1600 to 1815. Neither endpoint dates the people’s origin or disappearance. No artificial early phase is invented from those map dates.

The conference abstract is a report by Jean Brickey of Ewamian Aboriginal Corporation and Alice Buhrich of James Cook University. It is not a full excavation report and supplies no absolute ages for scars or grooves.
Only publicly described cultural features are summarized; no restricted site coordinates or knowledge is added.
The community page’s claim of uniquely successful resistance across all Australia is not reproduced.
The State Library’s no-known-speakers assessment is dated 2020 and is not represented as a verified present-day speaker count.
The native title page’s ambiguous area typography and broad legal generalizations are excluded. The card describes the community account, not individual legal advice.
Volcanic ages do not date Ewamian identity or occupation.
